text: The proof that irrational a, b exist with a^b rational uses √2^√2: if it is rational take a = b = √2, otherwise take a = √2^√2 and b = √2. Why is this proof called non-constructive?
choices: Because √2 is irrational and so cannot be written down exactly
Because it secretly uses induction with no base case
Because a^b is in fact never rational for these choices
Because it never determines which of the two cases holds, so it exhibits no definite witness
explanation: The argument invokes the law of excluded middle on '√2^√2 is rational or not' and concludes existence without deciding which case is real, so it produces no explicit witness pair — the hallmark of a non-constructive (classical) existence proof. Under the BHK interpretation, a constructive proof of ∃x P(x) must supply an actual witness. The other options misstate the mathematics.
